$comment: Vocabulary adapter map: the four legacy review verdict vocabularies (plus the v1.0 design draft) folded into the five canonical verdicts of ADDENDUM-HARDENING section 15. This file is DATA, not a JSON Schema. Canonical prose: v5 lane 4 section 5.3. Enforced by tests/firewall/review-verdict-adapter.test.js.

rules.note: An unknown token is not silently downgraded to PASS. An ambiguous token is not guessed: the adapter returns ambiguous:true with the candidate set and a human resolves it.

sources.description: v1.0 design package doc 08, superseded draft vocabulary

rows.note: The only source token in any vocabulary that reaches REPLAN_REQUIRED, and it comes from a design draft rather than a running pipeline.
Demoted to PASS; the warning survives as findings[] entries with their own severity, so no information is lost.
The only source token that reaches BLOCK.
Stage verdicts are conjunctive: a mission-level PASS needs SPEC_PASS and QUALITY_PASS together. This row maps the token only; combining the two stages is the caller's job.

The only row that splits. SPEC_FAIL means either the implementation falls short of the spec (REPAIR_REQUIRED) or the requirement itself is contradictory or unclear (INTENT_REVIEW_REQUIRED). The two are not distinguishable from the token, so the adapter must NOT classify it: return ambiguous:true and escalate to a human.
Conjunctive with SPEC_PASS, see the SPEC_PASS row.

unreachable_verdicts.INTENT_REVIEW_REQUIRED: No legacy token maps here unambiguously. The existing pipeline has no vocabulary for 'the requirement itself is wrong' and has been folding those cases into SPEC_FAIL. This is a vocabulary gap before it is a code gap.
unreachable_verdicts.REPLAN_REQUIRED: Reached only from the superseded v1.0 draft token 'replan'. No running reviewer emits it today.
